entities.name: Basilica of St. Michael, Bordeaux
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Basilica of Saint-Michel in Bordeaux (French: Basilique Saint-Michel de Bordeaux), a Gothic masterpiece begun in 1350 and completed in the 16th century in the Saint-Michel quarter of Bordeaux, is one of the largest Gothic churches in southwestern France — notable for its detached bell tower (the Flèche de Saint-Michel, 114 meters tall), the highest structure in southern France and the second highest in France after Chartres until the construction of the Eiffel Tower — and for the extraordinary mummified bodies (momies de la Crypte Saint-Michel) discovered in its charnel house in the 18th century and exhibited for several centuries.

Saint-Michel Bordeaux represents Bordeaux's medieval prosperity as a commercial city under both English (the Duchy of Aquitaine, controlled by the English Crown from 1152 to 1453 through Henry II's marriage to Eleanor of Aquitaine) and later French sovereignty. The church was built in the Flamboyant Gothic style — the final, most ornate phase of French Gothic — reflecting the economic wealth generated by Bordeaux's wine trade and Atlantic commerce. The detached campanile-style bell tower, built separately from the church in the Italianate campanile tradition (like the Leaning Tower of Pisa's relationship to Pisa Cathedral), was one of the most distinctive architectural choices in medieval southwestern France.

The Saint-Michel quarter historically housed Bordeaux's artisans, Jewish community, and immigrant populations — it is today one of Bordeaux's most multicultural and lively neighborhoods. The church was classified as a UNESCO World Heritage Site component as part of the Pilgrimage Routes to Santiago de Compostela (Saint-Michel was on a route for pilgrims traveling through southwestern France). The famous mummified bodies in the crypt attracted scientific and popular attention from the 18th century.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Basilica of Saint-Michel Bordeaux — Flamboyant Gothic masterpiece with southwestern France's tallest medieval tower, site of famous mummified remains, and UNESCO World Heritage component on the Santiago pilgrimage routes — is one of France's historically significant Gothic religious monuments.
